candidates.excerpt: MOSES LAKE, Wash. — Port of Moses Lake commissioners have approved a contract to build a new rail line connecting the port to the Columbia Basin Railroad. The Hagadone News Network reports that commissioners approved a $31.75 million contract with Martinus Rail LLC North America to build the connection at their meeting on Monday, Oct. 26. Construction could begin as early as next month, with completion projected in spring 2028. The Northern Columbia Basin Rail Project, designed to restore rail service that was lost in 2009, will include construction of 4.7 miles of new railroad and improvements to 2.7 miles of existing track. The port estimates it will initially generate round-trip service for 10 cars per week, growing to a daily round trip by 2045. candidates.title: Can railroads hang on to this year’s traffic gains?
candidates.excerpt: Record high diesel fuel prices and tight trucking capacity have prompted shippers to shift freight from highway to rail, sending domestic intermodal volume up 8% this year and boosting some carload commodities, too. The question now is whether railroads can hang on to the traffic once fuel prices moderate and the trucking industry solves a capacity crunch related to more strict federal enforcement of driver regulations. Executives from the three publicly traded U.S. Class I railroads said last week that keeping the new business will hinge on service. But UP and NS executives still expect some of the freight to return to the highway. Union Pacific CEO Jim Vena noted that elevated fuel prices boost the cost advantage railroads already enjoy over trucking. candidates.title: Jade Pacific makes liner debut with Red Sea service
candidates.excerpt: A new Singapore-based container shipping company headed by former SeaLead executives has entered the liner trades with a service connecting India, Pakistan and Egypt’s Red Sea coast. Jade Pacific Line (JPL), established in April this year, has deployed the 1,100 teu Medkon Sia on a rotation linking Mundra, Nhava Sheva, Karachi and Sokhna before returning to Mundra. According to liner consultancy Linerlytica, the service commenced on September 25 and operates on an irregular 30- to 35-day rolling schedule rather than a fixed weekly frequency. The operation provides a direct connection between two of India’s largest container gateways, Pakistan’s principal port and Egypt’s Sokhna, which serves the Suez Canal corridor and the Egyptian hinterland. JPL is affiliated with Chinese-linked container operators Ocean Silk Line (OSL) and OVP Shipping, with OSL holding a 30% stake in the newly established company.

candidates.title: Nuclear ships only pay off under the IMO’s net-zero rules, UCL study finds
candidates.excerpt: Nuclear ships only pay off under the IMO’s net-zero rules, UCL study finds Nuclear propulsion can compete in container shipping only if an effective global emissions policy is in place and reactor costs fall sharply, according to new research from the UCL Energy Institute’s Shipping and Oceans Research Group. It is one of the most detailed total cost-of-ownership assessments of nuclear merchant shipping to date. The report, Nuclear Reactors for Merchant Shipping: A Total Cost of Ownership Assessment of a Low-Carbon Pathway, compares a large container ship (14,500 to 19,999 TEU) with nuclear propulsion against conventional fuel oil and dual-fuel ammonia vessels. It uses a literature review, interviews with five UK-based experts in law, insurance, classification, technology development and industry representation, and a cost model run with and without the IMO Net-Zero Framework (NZF). candidates.title: Commodity markets whip up railfreight gains
candidates.excerpt: Industrial output help U.S. railroads steel themselves against increasing demand and show some mettle amid uncertain economic conditions. For the week ending Oct. 17, total U.S. weekly rail traffic was 540,135 carloads and intermodal units, up 8.5% from the same week a year ago, according to the Association of American Railroads. Carloads totaled 232,120 units, up 3.5%, and intermodal volume of 308,015 containers and trailers was 12.6% better y/y. candidates.title: Union Pacific CFO to retire
candidates.excerpt: Chief Financial Officer Jennifer Hamann will retire in early 2027, Union Pacific (NYSE: UNP) has announced. Hamann, who joined Union Pacific in 1992, was named CFO in January 2020. She had previously held leadership roles in a broad range of areas, including finance, human resources, marketing and sales, investor relations, and corporate audit. “For 35 years, she led with integrity and heart, guiding our finances through historic challenges, executing our strategy, mentoring future leaders and representing Union Pacific across the industry,” UP Chief Executive Jim Vena said in release. “Jennifer was tough — she never said yes unless she believed it was the right thing to do for Union Pacific. She made this railroad stronger, and her contributions will be felt for generations.
